description: "What's the ticker for..." / "find the CIK for..." / "what's the LEI for..." / "what's the RxCUI for..." / "look up the ID for..." / "what is X's official identifier" / "who owns X" / "is X a subsidiary of Y", resolve a user-spoken NAME to the canonical/official identifiers other tools require as input. Use FIRST whenever you have a name but need an ID. SUPPORTED TYPES: "company" (cross-source identity spine: 10-digit CIK + ticker + company_name from SEC EDGAR, legal-entity LEI from GLEIF with parent/ultimate-parent/children ownership when the LEI resolves, and security FIGI from OpenFIGI, by exact ticker map when a ticker is implied, and otherwise by name search, so NON-EQUITY instruments that never have a ticker (municipal and corporate bonds, notes, authority debt) DO resolve here; when a name matches more than one instrument it asserts nothing and returns `figi_candidates` to pick from, which is the correct answer to an issuer name that does not identify a single bond; every identifier is labelled with the source that established it, and an identifier that could NOT be resolved is stated explicitly under `unresolved` rather than omitted, accepts ticker, CIK, ISIN, LEI, or company name as input; an ISIN like "CH0038863350" resolves to the LEGAL ENTITY that issued the security via the GLEIF ISIN-to-LEI mapping, covering non-US issuers EDGAR cannot reach), "drug" (returns RxCUI + ingredient + brand from RxNorm + pipeworx://rxnorm/concept/{rxcui} citation; accepts brand or generic name). LEI/FIGI enrichment degrades gracefully, if GLEIF or OpenFIGI is unavailable, the EDGAR identifiers still return. Each call cascades through several lookup endpoints internally, using resolve_entity replaces 2-3 manual lookups.

country.description: OPTIONAL ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the country whose business register you mean ("NO", "FI", "JP", "GB", "FR", "EE", "BR"). Narrows the national-register fan-out and is often the difference between the right company and a US namesake, "Apple" with country "NO" is a Norwegian company, not Apple Inc. Omitting it searches every register we can name, which is the right default when you do not know. A bare number with a non-US country is that country's register number, never read as an SEC CIK (a 10-digit number still is). company only; ignored for drug.

type.description: Entity type: "company", "drug" or "lei" (a 20-character LEI; "company" also recognises an LEI by its check digits).

value.description: For company: ticker (AAPL), CIK (0000320193 or 320193), LEI (HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394), or name. A bare number is read as an SEC CIK only as 320193 or 0000320193; with a non-US `country`, or with 8-9 digits starting with 0 (a Companies House number), it is not a CIK and is not asserted as one. A bare number of 7 digits or fewer sent without `country` is always read as an SEC CIK, so a short register number (for example an Irish CRO or a US state filing number) that equals a real CIK will resolve to that SEC filer; send a non-US `country` with a foreign register number. A US state filing number cannot be resolved by number; search by company name instead. For drug: brand or generic name (e.g., "ozempic", "metformin"). Pass the ENTITY NAME ONLY, for a bond that is the ISSUER exactly as printed ("NEW YORK ST DORM AUTH"), never the question's full noun phrase ("NEW YORK ST DORM AUTH revenue bonds"): the FIGI lookup matches instrument names, so trailing security-class words match nothing.

name: resolve_entity

alternates.description: Entities that share the typed string with the entity in `ids`, in ONE fixed order for the same input (SEC registrants first when the basis is "sec_ticker_rival_name", then register rows by score, register_key, register_id), slimmed to who and where (the full rows are in `candidates`). For an exact ticker they are lookalikes of the symbol and do not make the answer ambiguous; for "sec_ticker_word" and "sec_name" they are the rivals the registers hold.

basis.description: Only on the two SEC rows of a "sec_ticker_rival_name" answer: which claim this registrant has on the string, the ticker or the name.

candidates.description: Rivals, best first. Populated on "ambiguous" and on "matched" alike. Register rows come from the register search; SEC registrants whose name matches (register_key "US-SEC-EDGAR", register_id the CIK, `cik` set) are added at the END, from the SEC leg: they were NOT part of the match scoring, their `score` is computed apart, and they never change `match_status` or what is asserted (fleet #4574).

cik.description: SEC rows only (register_key "US-SEC-EDGAR"): the registrant's 10-digit CIK, the same value as `register_id`. Fleet #4574.

country.description: ISO-2 of the REGISTER, not of the company's operations.

data_as_of.description: That register's own snapshot date, per row, so a stale country is visible.

detail_tool.description: The live pack tool that returns the full record, e.g. "brreg-no:brreg_no_get_entity".

id_round_trips.description: Whether `register_id`, sent back to resolve_entity as `value`, resolves to this same entity. true: the LEI (GLEIF rows), a CIK (US-SEC-EDGAR rows), and the BR, AU, PE, SG and LV register ids. false: DISPLAY-ONLY here, because these registers are not searched by id: a bare number sent back is not asserted as an SEC CIK when it has leading zeros and 8-9 digits (a GB company number) or comes with a non-US `country` (fleet #4522), and otherwise answers "no such SEC registrant". `detail_tool` names where such an id does go.

lei.description: From the GLEIF crosswalk when present. Never guessed from a name.

matched_name.description: The name row that matched, exactly as the publisher spells it.

register.description: Publisher + dataset, e.g. "Brønnøysund Register Centre, Enhetsregisteret". Never a URL or filename.

register_id.description: The native id in the register's own canonical formatting.

register_key.description: Stable machine slug for the register.

registration_status.description: GLEIF rows only: the LEI RECORD's lifecycle (ISSUED/LAPSED/RETIRED/...). A DIFFERENT fact from `status`, a lapsed LEI is unmaintained reference data about a company that may well still trade.

score.description: 0-1, assigned centrally. An adapter never grades itself.

sec_name_match.description: SEC rows only: how the SEC leg reached this registrant. "asserted": it is `ids.cik`. "withheld": it is `cik_withheld`, a name match not asserted. "sec_listed": SEC's own name list names it for the typed string (`sec_alternatives`).

status_raw.description: The register's own status word, verbatim and unglossed.

ticker.description: SEC rows only: the ticker SEC lists for that CIK today, when it lists one. A superseded registrant carries none.

cik_withheld.description: A CIK that came back from a FUZZY SEC name match and is NOT asserted, because the spine matched a stronger non-US candidate, or `match_status` is "ambiguous" or "incomplete" and the SEC hit was not an exact ticker, CIK or legal name (fleet #3606). The number is here so a caller who wanted the US filer can still use it; what changed is that we no longer claim it IS the answer. Also carries the CIK reading of a bare number that is not a CIK in either form EDGAR uses (fleet #4522): `resolved` is false, `company_name_withheld` is SEC's name for that CIK, and `unresolved.cik` says why. See `unresolved.cik` for the reason.

company_name_withheld.description: The company name of a FUZZY SEC name match that is NOT asserted, withheld together with `cik_withheld`. See `unresolved.cik`.

fanout_incomplete.description: Present IFF at least one register in `searched[]` carried an `error`, set even when `match_status` stayed "ambiguous". `withheld_match` is the candidate this call declined to ASSERT because a register was missing, carried rather than discarded so a caller who accepts the caveat can still use it.

figi_withheld.description: A FIGI that is NOT asserted. Either it matched this name in OpenFIGI (`figi_match: "name_search"`) while `match_status` is "incomplete", a name search cannot tell a company apart from a security carrying its name, and the registers that would have settled it are the ones we could not ask, or it is a `ticker_map` FIGI whose ticker came from a FUZZY SEC name match that is itself withheld (`cik_withheld`), so the mapping inherits the doubt. A `ticker_map` FIGI from an EXACT SEC hit (a real ticker, a CIK, an exact legal name) is never withheld. Carried so a caller who accepts the caveat can use it; see `unresolved.figi`.

ids.description: Every identifier established: cik, ticker, company_name, lei, figi, isin, cusip, register_id, register_country. A key absent here appears in `unresolved` with a reason, never silently dropped.

lei_record.description: Present when the input was an LEI GLEIF holds: GLEIF's own record, verbatim. `active` is true only when `entity_status` is "ACTIVE" and `registration_status` is "ISSUED"; a LAPSED or RETIRED LEI has `active: false` and the sentence in `notes` says so. A lapsed LEI is unmaintained reference data, not evidence the company stopped trading.

registration_status.description: ISSUED, LAPSED, RETIRED, ANNULLED, MERGED, DUPLICATE, PENDING_TRANSFER, ... as GLEIF states it.

lei_withheld.description: A LEI that is NOT asserted: it matched the bare string exactly in GLEIF, but `match_status` is "ambiguous" or "incomplete" so the registers cannot say which company that string means, and a GLEIF hit on the same string is the same guess from another register. `relationships` is withheld with it. A LEI from an exact SEC hit, or from a complete legal name carrying its legal form, is never withheld. See `unresolved.lei`.

match_basis.description: What `ids.cik` rests on, present whenever a CIK is asserted or withheld on this basis. "sec_ticker": the typed string is exactly the ticker symbol of one listed security, and it is not also the issuer's own first word; this settles the answer whatever the registers hold. "sec_ticker_word": also a ticker, but the typed word is the start of the issuer's name (Bolt, Uber), so register entities with that name are real rivals. "sec_name": a name match in SEC's company list. "sec_name_normalized": the typed name EQUALS the registrant's name in SEC's company list once a leading "The", punctuation and the Inc./Corp./Co./Ltd. spelling are set aside ("The Coca-Cola Company" equals COCA COLA CO), and exactly one SEC registrant has that name; nothing merely similar is guessed, and two registrants with the same normalised name assert neither (they are listed under `sec_alternatives`). "sec_cik": the caller supplied the CIK. "sec_ticker_rival_name": the string is the ticker of one SEC registrant AND the name of a different one (HP is Helmerich & Payne's ticker and the name of HP INC, ticker HPQ); neither is asserted, `resolved` is false, `match_status` is "ambiguous", and both head `alternates`. "lei_sec_name_state": SEC's own record for the CIK carries the same legal name and the same US state of incorporation as the LEI: the input was that LEI (see `sec_registrant`), or a company name that found no CIK in SEC's lists but whose exact GLEIF legal-name LEI could be confirmed this way. "sec_ticker_unchecked": the string is a ticker symbol, but SEC's registrant-name index did not answer, so whether it is also another registrant's name could not be checked; nothing is asserted, `resolved` is false, `match_status` is "ambiguous", the ticker holder is under `cik_withheld`, and a retry completes it. "sec_name_unique_issuer" (only when SEC issuer rule v2 is enabled): the typed name EQUALS the title of exactly one ticker-bearing SEC issuer once case, punctuation, a leading "The" and the legal suffix are set aside (`sec_issuer_index.step` "rule_v2_1"); the other issuers the name reaches are in `sec_alternatives`. "sec_name_leading_issuer" (rule v2 only): the name is two or more words, is not equal to any title, and is the LEADING whole words of the title of exactly ONE ticker-bearing SEC issuer ("jpmorgan chase" is the start of JPMORGAN CHASE & CO; step "leading_phrase"), that issuer being listed on a primary US exchange with no other primary-listed issuer containing the words; if two or more issuers start with those words this basis is not used. "sec_name_leading_word" (rule v2 only): the same, for a ONE-word name ("costco" is the start of COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP; step "leading_word"); the weaker of the two, since a single word is more often generic. "sec_name_contains_issuer" (rule v2 only): the name is not equal to any title but appears as whole words in the title of exactly one ticker-bearing SEC issuer, or of several of which exactly one is listed on a primary US exchange and the rest are OTC or unlisted (steps "rule_v2_2" and "rule_v2_3"); a weaker claim than "sec_name_unique_issuer", to be read as "did you mean". Inputs under 4 alphanumeric characters never get a leading or contains basis. "sec_former_name" (rule v2 only): the typed name is a former name of exactly one SEC issuer (`sec_issuer_index.matched_former_name`) and no current SEC title carries it.

match_explanation.description: Plain words. Always present when the spine ran, and required on "ambiguous" and "no_match".

match_scoring.description: The margin rule's own inputs, so a caller can see WHY it fell where it did.

match_status.description: The headline to branch on. "matched" is ONE entity: a national-register match, or, when `match_basis` is "sec_ticker", a typed string that is exactly the ticker symbol of one listed security (the register search's own verdict is then kept in `register_match_status` and its lookalikes in `alternates`). "ambiguous" is an ANSWER, not a failure: two companies matched the name equally well and both are in `candidates`. "no_match" means every register in `searched` was asked and none carried it. "incomplete" means one of them could NOT be asked (it carries an `error` in `searched[]`), so the candidate set is short by an unknown amount and no id is asserted, distinct from "ambiguous" because a RETRY is what resolves it, not a narrower query; `fanout_incomplete` names the unreachable registers and carries, under `withheld_match`, the candidate that would have been returned on a complete fan-out.

predecessor.description: Present only when SEC's own records show this CIK is the SUCCESSOR registrant of another (a holding-company reorganisation moved the listed security to a new registrant). `cik` / `company_name` name the registrant that holds the earlier filings and XBRL history; `last_period_end` is the period end of the last periodic report the predecessor filed on its own (not counting a report filed jointly under both CIKs, whose facts sit under the successor), i.e. where the predecessor's own facts series ends. Never inferred from a name, and the two registrants' data are never merged.

basis.description: "sec_8k12b_joint_filing": the successor filed an 8-K12B (SEC's succession notice) and, within days, a registration-statement amendment jointly with this registrant. "sec_8k12b_cover_file_number": the 8-K12B cover prints this registrant's Commission file number, which SEC holds under this CIK.

evidence.description: The two SEC records the link rests on: the successor's 8-K12B (SEC's formal succession notice) and a registration-statement amendment filed jointly by both registrants, with the registration numbers each filed under.

register_match_status.description: Present only when `match_status` was settled by an exact ticker rather than by the registers: the register search's own verdict, verbatim. It never changes which security the ticker names.

register_withheld.description: Present only when register-pairing rule v2 is enabled and withheld a register entity: the national-register entity the register search matched for this name, which is NOT asserted under `ids` because the answer asserts an SEC CIK, the register is not US, and nothing ties the two (the register row's LEI is not `ids.lei`, and the register id is not that LEI). It is a same-name entity in another country's register, not evidence about this company. The same row stays in `candidates`; `unresolved.register_id` carries `reason`. Pass `country` equal to `register_country` to ask about that register's entity, which is then kept.

related.description: Register entities that had collapsed into the withheld one (previously top-level `related`).

registers.description: The matched entity as every register that carries it, the match (flagged `matched: true`) plus anything that collapsed into it. A Companies House number AND the LEI that crosswalks to it are the SAME answer, not rivals.

country.description: ISO-2 of the REGISTER, not of the company's operations.

data_as_of.description: That register's own snapshot date, per row, so a stale country is visible.

detail_tool.description: The live pack tool that returns the full record, e.g. "brreg-no:brreg_no_get_entity".

id_round_trips.description: Whether `register_id`, sent back to resolve_entity as `value`, resolves to this same entity. true: the LEI (GLEIF rows), a CIK (US-SEC-EDGAR rows), and the BR, AU, PE, SG and LV register ids. false: DISPLAY-ONLY here, because these registers are not searched by id: a bare number sent back is not asserted as an SEC CIK when it has leading zeros and 8-9 digits (a GB company number) or comes with a non-US `country` (fleet #4522), and otherwise answers "no such SEC registrant". `detail_tool` names where such an id does go.

matched_name.description: The name row that matched, exactly as the publisher spells it.

register.description: Publisher + dataset, e.g. "Brønnøysund Register Centre, Enhetsregisteret". Never a URL or filename.

register_id.description: The native id in the register's own canonical formatting.

register_key.description: Stable machine slug for the register.

registration_status.description: GLEIF rows only: the LEI RECORD's lifecycle (ISSUED/LAPSED/RETIRED/...). A DIFFERENT fact from `status`, a lapsed LEI is unmaintained reference data about a company that may well still trade.

score.description: 0-1, assigned centrally. An adapter never grades itself.

status_raw.description: The register's own status word, verbatim and unglossed.

related.description: Entities that collapsed INTO the match, each carrying `collapsed_by`.

country.description: ISO-2 of the REGISTER, not of the company's operations.

data_as_of.description: That register's own snapshot date, per row, so a stale country is visible.

detail_tool.description: The live pack tool that returns the full record, e.g. "brreg-no:brreg_no_get_entity".

id_round_trips.description: Whether `register_id`, sent back to resolve_entity as `value`, resolves to this same entity. true: the LEI (GLEIF rows), a CIK (US-SEC-EDGAR rows), and the BR, AU, PE, SG and LV register ids. false: DISPLAY-ONLY here, because these registers are not searched by id: a bare number sent back is not asserted as an SEC CIK when it has leading zeros and 8-9 digits (a GB company number) or comes with a non-US `country` (fleet #4522), and otherwise answers "no such SEC registrant". `detail_tool` names where such an id does go.

register.description: Publisher + dataset, e.g. "Brønnøysund Register Centre, Enhetsregisteret". Never a URL or filename.

register_id.description: The native id in the register's own canonical formatting.

register_key.description: Stable machine slug for the register.

registration_status.description: GLEIF rows only: the LEI RECORD's lifecycle (ISSUED/LAPSED/RETIRED/...). A DIFFERENT fact from `status`, a lapsed LEI is unmaintained reference data about a company that may well still trade.

score.description: 0-1, assigned centrally. An adapter never grades itself.

status_raw.description: The register's own status word, verbatim and unglossed.

resolved.description: At least one identifier was established. Read `match_basis` for WHAT the ids rest on and `unresolved` for what is missing; a company can be resolved in a national register with no CIK at all. When `match_status` is "matched" this is true. `resolved: true` with `match_status: "ambiguous"` is the one residual combination and it means exactly this: SEC named ONE filer on an exact hit that is also a name or word (`match_basis` "sec_ticker_word" or "sec_name", e.g. "Bolt", "Zoom"), and the registers hold rivals with the same name, listed under `alternates`. An exact ticker symbol ("AAPL") is never in that state, and a ticker that is also the name of a DIFFERENT registrant ("HP") is `resolved: false` with `match_basis` "sec_ticker_rival_name".

searched.description: EVERY register asked, with its own as-of date and row count. A register that could not be reached carries `error`, 0 rows with an error is "we could not ask", 0 rows without one is "nothing is there", and they are different answers.

sec_alternatives.description: EDGAR's other name-matching candidates: distinct companies, deduped by CIK, excluding this issuer's own share classes, surfaced instead of dropped so a caller can tell a genuinely CONTESTED name match from a clean one. When two or more SEC registrants have the SAME name once a leading "The", punctuation and Inc./Corp./Co./Ltd. spelling are set aside, no CIK is asserted and all of them are listed here (fleet #4550).

listing.description: Only on SEC issuer rule v2 rows: where the issuer is listed.

sec_issuer_index.description: Present only when SEC issuer rule v2 is enabled and was asked: how the rule decided and how fresh the index is. "step": rule_v2_1 (one ticker-bearing issuer's title equals the name), leading_phrase (a name of 2+ words is the leading whole words of exactly one primary-listed title), leading_word (the same for a one-word name), rule_v2_2 (one title contains it as whole words), rule_v2_3 (of several, one on a primary US exchange and the rest OTC or unlisted), former_name, superseded_title, ambiguous (nothing asserted; `candidates` lists the issuers the name reached), none. "available": false means the index could not be read, which is not evidence the company is absent. "data_as_of" is the SEC data date.

matched_listed.description: How many ticker-bearing SEC issuers (OTC included) the name reached, the asserted issuer included. 1 means no other; more than 1 means the others are under sec_alternatives or candidates, which list at most 10.

sec_registrant.description: Present when the input was an LEI: whether the legal entity is an SEC registrant. "found": `ids.cik` is asserted, the CIK whose SEC record carries the same legal name and the same US state of incorporation as the LEI (`match_basis` "lei_sec_name_state"). "none_found": SEC's registrant lookup and its company-name lookup both answered and matched no registrant with that legal name (a leading "The", punctuation and Inc./Corp./Co./Ltd. spelling are set aside), so `ids.cik` is absent and `unresolved.cik` says what was matched; it is not a statement that the entity is not an SEC registrant. Most LEIs are this. "not_established": it could not be settled, SEC did not answer, or a name match could not be confirmed against a state (every non-US jurisdiction), so no CIK is asserted; the unconfirmed CIK, if any, is under `cik_withheld`.

sources.description: Per-identifier provenance. Every key in `ids` has a matching key here.

successor.description: Present only when SEC's own records show this CIK is the PREDECESSOR of a successor registrant (the counterpart of `predecessor`). `cik` / `company_name` name the registrant that now holds the listed security and the filings after `succession_date`.

evidence.description: The two SEC records the link rests on: the successor's 8-K12B (SEC's formal succession notice) and a registration-statement amendment filed jointly by both registrants, with the registration numbers each filed under.

ticker_withheld.description: The ticker of a FUZZY SEC name match that is NOT asserted, withheld together with `cik_withheld` because it is the same guess. Carried so a caller who meant the US filer can still use it; see `unresolved.ticker`.

unresolved.description: Per-identifier reason an id could NOT be established, the honest twin of `ids`.
